newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends flat, money market rates up.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends flat, money market rates up.

text.p: The Romanian leu closed Tuesday unchanged at 5,750/800 to the dollar after inching down in early trading on an interbank market still faced by hard currency shortages.
"As the leu's downswing tapered off in recent days, some dollar sellers showed up. But interbank trading continued to be scarce," said a trader with one of the four dealer banks.
Latest central bank data showed a $221,500 interbank volume on Monday, when overall trading was $13.9 million.
Traders said the leu was likely to head lower towards 5,900 to the dollar by weekend.
"With recent tightening in the central bank's monetary policy, the dollar might test a resistance point near 6,000-6,200 lei," said another trader.

But most operators said the leu remained vulnerable over inflationary fears, while the market was anxious to get clues about the reform package which Romania's new centrist government is negotiating with the International Monetary Fund.

The Fund started talks with the new Bucharest leaders last week on resuming IMF loans suspended in 1996. On Thursday Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will announce the first details of the reform pledges made in exchange for renewed IMF funds.
Leu-dollar retail rates marked time at 6,000/200.
Short-term money market rates climbed towards 65 percent from some 60 percent in early trading with big players chasing leu funds.
